subtopics.title: Maritime and Territorial Disputes
subtopics.summary: A Pakistani naval vessel, PNS Hunain, collided with the Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata in the North Arabian Sea, and India lodged a diplomatic protest after calling the conduct unsafe. The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement on advance notice of military exercises is a confidence-building measure meant to reduce accidental escalation. The Falklands dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom has resurfaced over sovereignty and oil exploration, and the United States has moved to rename Lake Ontario, a step Canada opposed.

subtopics.title: International Conventions and Diplomacy
subtopics.summary: The European Commission President has proposed exploring an 'Associate Member' relationship that could let Canada take part more closely in selected EU frameworks without full membership. Under the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, 128 countries reached a consensus on a working definition of lethal autonomous weapons systems. CITES regulates international trade in endangered wild species through three appendices, and the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment govern the phase-out of ozone-depleting and hydrofluorocarbon substances.
facts: EU proposal to explore an 'Associate Member' relationship, illustrated with Canada
'Associate Membership' is not an established membership category under the EU's foundational treaties
Treaty revision would require all 27 EU Member States to agree

CITES species are listed in three appendices by conservation status and trade sensitivity
Montreal Protocol (1987) led to a 99% phase-out of controlled ozone-depleting substances; Kigali Amendment (2016) mandates phase-down of HFCs

subtopics.title: Governance, Standards and Schemes
subtopics.summary: The PM Vishwakarma scheme completed three years of implementation in September 2026 and supports artisans in 18 traditional trades. Registered Unrecognised Political Parties (RUPPs) are under scrutiny over political funding transparency, with the Election Commission of India registering parties under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 make IST the single mandatory time reference for official purposes, and Karnataka has granted Tulu additional administrative language status.
facts: PM Vishwakarma scheme is fully funded by the Government of India and runs from FY 2023-24 to FY 2027-28
Covers 18 traditional trades in rural and urban areas
Only one member per family can apply; applicant must be over 18 years of age
Applicants who benefited from PMEGP or PM Swanidhi in the past 5 years are not eligible
RUPPs are registered with ECI but have not acquired status of a recognised State or National Party
Section 29A RPA 1951: registration of political parties; Section 29C: contribution reports
Supreme Court in ADR v. Union of India (2024) struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme

IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of UTC and is based on 82.5 degrees East longitude
Tulu was granted status of additional administrative language in Karnataka; Tulu is not in the Eighth Schedule

subtopics.title: Economy, Energy and Urbanisation
subtopics.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves rose to a record high, moving the country to fourth place globally, with the rise linked to RBI concessional swap arrangements tied to FCNR(B) deposits. The Union Cabinet approved a scheme to promote new surface coal and lignite gasification projects, building on the National Coal Gasification Mission of 2021. The India Electric Mobility Index 2025 ranks States and UTs on EV progress, while the Kishau Multipurpose Dam and the Census Town criteria address water sharing and urbanisation.

subtopics.title: Science, Environment and Culture
subtopics.summary: CosmoCube and PRATUSH are proposed Indian and international missions for detecting the 21-cm signal from the early universe, while NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been launched to study dark energy and exoplanets. Five young orangutans rescued in Odisha were moved to a zoo, and orangutans are native only to Borneo and Sumatra. World Rhino Day on 22 September highlighted the five rhino species, and the 2024 National Film Awards were announced.

quizzes.title: Disputes at Sea, Land and Lake
quizzes.passage:
Several disputes over sea, land and naming drew attention this month. A Pakistani naval vessel, PNS Hunain, collided with the Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata in the North Arabian Sea. India described the conduct of the Pakistani vessel as unsafe, said the incident took place in international waters, and lodged a diplomatic protest. The episode became both a maritime and a diplomatic dispute. A similar collision had taken place in the Gulf of Aden in June 2011, involving INS Godavari and PNS Babur.

The two countries already have a bilateral agreement from 1991 that is meant to reduce the possibility of accidents between their naval platforms. It is a confidence-building measure intended to prevent misinterpretation of military activities.

Elsewhere, the long-running Falklands dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom has resurfaced, with disagreements over sovereignty and oil exploration around the islands. The United Kingdom says it has exercised continuous and peaceful authority over the islands, while Argentina considers British control illegitimate and refers to the territory as Las Malvinas. The islands are a British Overseas Territory.

In North America, the United States has moved to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Canada opposed the proposal, pointing to the name's Indigenous Wendat origins and its long use. Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes and lies between Ontario province and New York State.

questions.q: Under the 1991 India-Pakistan Agreement on Advance Notice of Military Exercises, what is the minimum distance that naval ships and submarines of the two countries should keep from each other while operating in international waters?
questions.explanation: Article 10 of the agreement says such ships and submarines should not approach within 3 nautical miles of each other in international waters.

questions.q: On which date was the 1991 India-Pakistan Agreement on Advance Notice of Military Exercises signed?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the agreement was signed on 6 April 1991.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement aims to reduce the possibility of accidents involving naval platforms of the two countries.
Reason (R): Naval ships and submarines of the two countries are allowed to approach within 3 nautical miles of each other while operating in international waters.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true because the agreement aims to reduce accidents, but R is false because Article 10 says such ships should not approach within 3 nautical miles.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Falklands Islands   ->   C. Links Lake Ontario with Lake Erie
II. Lake Ontario   ->   A. Establish internationally recognised rules of navigation
III. COLREGs   ->   D. Lie roughly 480 km from Argentina's eastern coast
IV. Welland Canal   ->   B. Smallest of the Great Lakes by surface area
questions.explanation: The Falklands lie roughly 480 km from Argentina's coast, Lake Ontario is the smallest Great Lake, COLREGs set navigation rules, and the Welland Canal links Lake Ontario to Lake Erie.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lake Ontario:
I. Lake Ontario is the largest of the five Great Lakes by surface area.
II. Lake Ontario does not border the state of Michigan.
III. The Niagara River is the principal source of water entering Lake Ontario.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Lake Ontario is the smallest of the five Great Lakes by surface area, so statement I is false, while II and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The COLREGs establish internationally recognised rules of navigation and collision avoidance for vessels at sea.
II. Argentina became independent from Spain in 1830.
III. Lake Ontario is the easternmost and final lake in the Great Lakes system.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because Argentina became independent from Spain in 1816.

questions.q: In the 2013 referendum held in the Falkland Islands, approximately what percentage of participating islanders voted to retain the islands' status as a British Overseas Territory? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that approximately 99.8% of participating islanders voted to retain British Overseas Territory status.

questions.q: As successor to the colonial possessions of which country in the region does Argentina argue that it inherited territorial claims over the Falkland Islands?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Argentina argues it inherited Spain's territorial claims as successor to Spanish colonial possessions in the region.

quizzes.title: Economy and Schemes: Key Numbers
quizzes.passage:
Several economic and infrastructure stories were in the news this month. The Union Cabinet approved a scheme to promote new surface coal and lignite gasification projects that produce syngas, building on the National Coal Gasification Mission launched in 2021. Gasification converts coal into a gaseous fuel instead of burning it directly, and the scheme is part of a wider national objective for coal gasification capacity by 2030. Eligible projects receive financial assistance on their plant and machinery, subject to ceilings for each project, each product and each entity.

In electric mobility, NITI Aayog and World Resources Institute India released the India Electric Mobility Index 2025. It evaluates how States and Union Territories are progressing towards electric mobility on a scale of 0 to 100, using three pillars: transport electrification progress, charging infrastructure readiness and EV research and innovation. Delhi retained the highest overall position.

A long-pending inter-state project, the Kishau Multipurpose Dam, has also moved forward. It is planned on the Tons River, a tributary of the Yamuna, and several States and Union Territories have reached agreement on its implementation.

Urban statistics were discussed too. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs told a Parliamentary panel that the criteria for identifying a Census Town may no longer reflect India's changing urbanisation. A Census Town is treated as urban for Census purposes even though it may not be a formally notified urban local body.

Finally, India's foreign exchange reserves reached a record high, a rise linked mainly to inflows through RBI's concessional swap arrangements tied to FCNR(B) deposits.

questions.q: What percentage of the cost of the water component will the Union Government provide as Central Assistance for the Kishau Multipurpose Dam Project? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The Union Government provides 90% of the cost of the water component, and the remaining 10% is shared by the participating States/UT.

questions.q: Up to what percentage of expenditure on plant and machinery will the government provide as financial assistance under the new coal and lignite gasification scheme? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the government will provide financial assistance of up to 20% of expenditure on plant and machinery.

questions.q: How many performance indicators does the India Electric Mobility Index 2025 use to evaluate States and Union Territories?
questions.explanation: The index is evaluated on a 0-100 scale across 16 performance indicators.

questions.q: How many States/UTs are participating in the Kishau Multipurpose Dam Project?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists six participating States/UT: Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

questions.q: What minimum population must a settlement have to qualify as a Census Town under the criteria introduced for the 1981 Census? (in persons)
questions.explanation: A Census Town must have at least 5,000 persons, along with an occupational and a population density condition.

questions.q: After the recent rise, what global rank did India attain in foreign exchange reserves? (ordinal)
questions.explanation: India moved to 4th position globally, ahead of Russia and after China, Japan and Switzerland.

questions.q: What weight, in per cent, does the Transport Electrification Progress pillar carry in the India Electric Mobility Index 2025? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The transport electrification pillar carries 50% of the index, with charging infrastructure at 30% and EV research and innovation at 20%.
